svg.aria-label: A vertical timeline, The Keepers of the Fire, from 1959 to 2026. 1959: MIT Tech Model Railroad Club writes down 'hack' and 'hacker'. 1971: the 2600-hertz tone and blue boxes; Esquire publishes Secrets of the Little Blue Box. 1975: the Homebrew Computer Club meets in Menlo Park. 1981: the Chaos Computer Club is founded in Berlin. 1983: Richard Stallman announces the GNU Project. 1984: Steven Levy writes down the hacker ethic; 2600 magazine begins; the CCC's Btx hack. 1986: the Mentor writes the Hacker Manifesto in Phrack; Congress passes the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. 1988: the Morris Worm; Cliff Stoll traces the Cuckoo's Egg. 1990: Operation Sundevil and the founding of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. 1991: Linus Torvalds releases Linux; Phil Zimmermann releases PGP. 1993: the first DEF CON; the Clipper chip fight and the Cypherpunks. 1998: L0pht testifies to the US Senate. 2016 to 2026: Hack the Pentagon, bug bounties, and the AI era.
svg.text: The Keepers of the Fire
Sixty-seven years, one unbroken line — from a clubroom to the machines that hack
The word is written down

The phone is a computer

The other shore

The ethic, and the quarterly
Levy writes the ethic down; 2600 begins; the CCC’s Btx hack
The manifesto, and the law
The Mentor writes it in Phrack; Congress passes the CFAA
The first worm, the first catch
The Morris Worm; Cliff Stoll traces the Cuckoo’s Egg

The first DEF CON; the Clipper fight; the Cypherpunks
Speaking truth to power

The government says please
Hack the Pentagon: the first federal bug bounty
The machines join the fire
Autonomous agents find and write exploits — the story continues
